title: Armstrong
html_source:
The significance of this name is not known (Gifford & Seidman, p30). That readers and critics would delve so deep to ascertain its relevance illustrates the reader response to Ulysses.

Ulysses‘ Homeric parallels imply there are no actual Homeric figures and “although Ulysses contains a wealth of detail concerning Dublin and people’s lives there, the novel is hardly a realistic work of fiction; indeed, rather than creating "the illusion of reality,” these details become a sort of end in themselves, such as one finds in the art-form of the collage.“ (Ross C Murfin in A Companion to James Joyce’s Ulysses referring to the work of Wolfgang Iser).

Murfin adds how we look outward for Homeric parallels as well as inward to our own personal experiences. Merging the two is the task of the reader of Ulysses.
